data.name: Realms of Arkania 1 - Blade of Destiny Classic
data.detailed_description:
Blade of Destiny (1992) is the first part of the glorious Realms of Arkania Trilogy...

An Orc army stands ready to attack Arkania's villages and towns. The only hope of saving the land lies in the legendary Blade of Destiny. Can you find this magical weapon in time to stop the siege? A rich and detailed adventure that will engage your mind and challenge your imaginations.

The Realms of Arkania Trilogy

The Realms of Arkania games (Blade of Destiny, Star Trail and Shadows of Riva) deliver a prime example of the classical European fantasy universe. Based on Germany's most popular pen & paper role playing game, it was also the first German computer RPG series to get widely recognized outside of its home country. To this day it holds a stable hardcore fanbase that loves the games for their comprehensive adaption of the pen & paper ruleset and the believable medieval fantasy setting.

reviews.review:
Wizardry X Oregon Trail, a really cool and fun combination. The character creating and immersion from the get go is great, extremely detailed character creation and stats that impact combat and roleplay situations. I really appreciate that the roleplaying aspects are seemingly equally as important as the combat and dungeon crawling here, it makes this game distinctly unique from its contemporaries.

However, heres the big issue with this game; those deep stats and character creation elements, yeah literally like 90% of those stats are meaningless. This game has 40 spells, and only about 10 of them are usable, and not "Useful", usable, the rest are entirely redundant and pointless. This is also true for the plethora of stats, it goes beyond some being better than others and moreso that barrels of them do quite literally nothing. This has its upsides ( I guess ) as it makes the stat distribution and such easier than the overwhelming goliath it appears to be at first. But if you dont instantly figure out whats a total waste of time to invest in, I could imagine it being incredibly annoying to dump stats into say, riding or animal caring, or even treat wounds (Something you would think would be good) and just ruining your builds for no reason.

Thankfully the combat is extremely basic and barebones, which isnt great but it makes the overwhelming confusing amount of useless stats easier to manage, as its pretty hard to actually struggle with the combat. Again, the roleplaying and immersion is where the fun is here, but you can kind of pretend its deep due to the hours you will have to spend assigning numbers to stats.

The gameplay loop here is good on paper, you do whatever you like travelling through towns and talking to people, while searching for map pieces and looting dungeons. It can be satisfying tracking down the map pieces as you naturally explore but there is 2 big issues.

1. Its incredibly repetetive and bit lame that you've got about a 80% chance that your current end goal will just give you names of other end goals instead of anything. So sometimes you will go literal hours of, "Go find this guy" then you find him and he says "Go find this guy" about 5 times in a row until you finally get a map piece. There are a few map pieces that require a fight or dungeon, but way to much of the main quest is just directly going from person to person.

2. This game is fucking BROKEN. There are many of the map pieces that hinge on really obtuse bullshit that you can permanently miss or that can be forever lost due to a bug. I had 3 of my map pieces locked away, and had a total nightmare of a time figuring out to get the Unicorn. They clearly knew this since you dont even need to get all the map pieces and they have that Unicorn as an anti softlock, but its stressful and annoying how easy it is to hardlock your game.

Overall this game lives or dies on the vibes. Ultimately its as wide as an ocean as deep as a puddle, but its pseudo depth and actual simplicity kind of makes it a "Comfy" experience. Its sold to you in its premise and manuals as this super awesome tabletop experience, so if you expect that you will be incredibly disappointed. But if you just want some lite roleplaying fun, this provides that.
